chapter: Porgy and Bess and Varsity Show
title: Buck's ragtime piano and his influence on Tatum and Peterson
summary: Buck turned classics into ragtime, giving points to Art Tatum and Oscar Peterson; neither considered splitting after 40 years together.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Making ragtime out of classics. Like "Souvenir from Woolworths," "Kiss me Again," Sextet from "Lucia di Lammermoer," "Hearts and Flowers," and "Clare de Lune," "Kiss me Again." Hit take all classics and make ragtime music out of them, you know.
He probably had an influence on a lot of pianists.
Yeah, yes he did. He did, I agree with you there, a lot of influence on most of the best ones. He taught some of the best ones, too. And Art Tatum /and wasn't no slouch now there was Oscar Peterson.

No, he didn't teach nobody, they just got points from him. What makes them what they are is what they heard him do. Something that they heard him do. Oh, he could play the piano awhile. I know you've heard a record of his somewhere.
Were there other outlets for Buck? Did Buck want to go off on his own as just a pianist? Did he ever consider that?
No, I don't think he ever considered that. Not that I ever considered going off alone without him. That's
because we were together so long. Forty years is a long time to be together, you know that. We stuck it out.
